Subject: Follow-up: Private VPC data handling questions

Hi Marissa / Vivek -

Thanks again for the demo today. A couple of follow-ups from my security team that we need to clarify before progressing to a technical review:

- Does any customer prompt text or inference token data leave our VPC or go to Redwood-managed services?
- What data is persisted for debugging/metrics (request logs, traces, KV cache)? How long is it retained and who can access it?
- Are there any outbound egress connections to public services during inference (e.g., for telemetry, model pulls)? We need a list of endpoints/ports and an option for fully restricted egress.
- For our regulated workflows we may require an on-prem / air-gapped deployment - is that supported and what constraints apply?

Can you share a current data flow diagram and a short summary of controls (KMS, audit logs, network boundary options)?

Thanks,
Alice Chen
Head of Security, ACME Health

From: Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>

Date: 2026-11-02T09:04:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Private VPC data handling questions

Hi Alice -

Great questions, and thanks for flagging them. Attached is an updated data flow diagram (acme_private_vpc_dataflow_v2.pdf) that reflects our Private/VPC deployment options. High-level answers below; Rishi and Neha are looped in for the technical details.

- Token/data egress: In our Private deployment, inference requests enter your VPC via a private endpoint; tokens are processed on compute nodes inside the VPC. By default we do not mirror prompt/token payloads to Redwood-managed public services. Model artifacts can be hosted on a customer-controlled object store if required.

- Persistence: We persist minimal metadata for routing/observability (request id, timestamps, processing status). Call-level logs and traces are configurable - default is ephemeral (48 hours) but we can configure retention and disable storage. KV cache is kept in-memory by default; persistent cache is opt-in and can be placed in your managed storage.

- Egress & endpoints: We support private NAT/NLB configurations and static allowlists for outbound connections. We can disable outbound egress entirely (air-gapped) for an on-prem deployment; for VPC deployments we document required endpoints/ports - see attached and the linked security doc.

- On-prem/air-gapped: We support a packaged on-prem deployment for full air-gap scenarios; there are additional operational constraints (hardware minimums, offline model provisioning process, and limited automatic updates). Neha can share the checklist.

Next steps:
1) Rishi / Neha to provide a short technical note (endpoints, ports, KMS model) by EOD Thursday.
2) Schedule a 60-min architecture review with your infra/security team - propose Nov 5 or Nov 8.

Attaching: acme_private_vpc_dataflow_v2.pdf, redwood_vpc_security_summary.pdf

Best,
Marissa Cole
Account Executive, Redwood Inference

Marissa / Rishi -

Quick clarifying items from our infra team after reviewing the diagram:

1) If a customer chooses the default in-memory KV cache, are there any background snapshots or replication to Redwood control plane? We need assurance nothing is persisted outside our VPC unless explicitly configured.
2) For audit logs - can they be delivered to our Splunk/CloudWatch directly (push model) rather than stored in any Redwood bucket?
3) Model weights: will any model weights or checkpoints be pulled from Redwood public registries at runtime, or can we provision them into our private object store ahead of time?

Also: can you provide concrete CIDR/IP ranges and ports for the minimal set of outbound allowlist rules if we need limited egress (we run strict firewalling)?

Thanks,
Bob Rivera
Director, Infrastructure - ACME Health

From: Rishi Malhotra <rishi.malhotra@redwood.com>
To: Bob Rivera <bob.rivera@acmehealth.com>; Marissa Cole <marissa.cole@redwood.com>
Cc: Neha Kapoor <neha.kapoor@redwood.com>; Vivek Kulkarni <vivek.kulkarni@redwood.com>
Date: 2026-11-04T09:00:00-07:00
Subject: Re: Follow-up: Private VPC data handling questions

Hi Bob / team -

Thanks - answers inline below and a short technical summary attached.

1) KV cache: Default is in-memory on the inference nodes and is not snapshotted or replicated to Redwood's control plane. Persistent cache is opt-in and can be backed by a customer-managed object store or Redis inside your VPC. No background snapshots to Redwood-managed storage unless you enable the feature and grant us access.

2) Audit logs: We can stream audit and request logs directly to your logging endpoint (Splunk/CloudWatch) via secure push or place logs in a customer-managed bucket in your account. We do not retain logs in Redwood-managed buckets for Private deployments unless requested.

3) Model weights: For Private and on-prem deployments you can pre-provision model weights into your object store. Redwood also supports hosting model artifacts in a private registry inside the VPC; runtime pulls are local. We do not reach out to public registries from your inference nodes when the private option is selected.

Egress/allowlist:
- Required minimal outbound: our control-plane handshake only (optional) - but for fully private deployments this can be disabled. If enabled, endpoints are: 10.200.5.0/24 (management plane in the customer's VPC) and several static IPs we provide per deployment. We will provide final CIDR/IP list as part of the deployment runbook.

Security controls: KMS-integrated key management (customer keys in KMS/HSM), mutual TLS for control-plane endpoints, and RBAC for who can request logs/model access.

Attached: redwood_vpc_security_summary.pdf (short checklist). See also: https://docs.redwood.com/security/private-vpc-architecture

If helpful, I can join the architecture review - proposing Nov 5 11am PT.

Regards,
Rishi Malhotra
Solutions Engineer, Redwood Inference
